newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway shares backtrack, strong crown takes toll.
newsitem.headline: Norway shares backtrack, strong crown takes toll.

text.p: Norwegian shares backtracked on Friday as sentiment turned negative on export-oriented companies due to the relentless bull rally in the crown, which continued despite the Central Bank cutting key interest rates for the second time in as many days.
Strong U.S. payrolls data also took prices down a peg, although dealers said a correction in the market was expected following heavy gains so far this year.
The Total share index managed to hold above the psychological 1,000-point mark first breached on Wednesday to close 0.74 percent down at 1,001.05 points.
Turnover was a bumper 2.08 billion crowns, with trade in industrial giant Norsk Hydro accounting for 20 percent of turnover at 412 million crowns.

The Central Bank shaved 25 basis points off both the overnight deposit and overnight lending rates to 3.25 and 5.25 percent respectively. On Thursday it reduced both rates by 50 basis points in an attempt to dampen the crown's steep climb.
Shares in metals producer Elkem and forestry group Norske Skogindustrier were hit by the appreciating currency, sinking six and 11 crowns to 105 and 199 crowns respectively.
